thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert — GPU serving pool us-west-2-gpu showing sustained queue growth > 90% and request latency spikes. Autoscaler reported failure to add nodes (max_replicas reached). Severity: P1.

maria: Seeing 5k requests queued, tail latency 2.4s -> 12s for generation routes. Customers impacted: some realtime chat apps and a few enterprise inference endpoints.

alex: paging. I'm oncall. immediate ask: can someone confirm autoscaler max? where are the logs?

chris: Autoscaler config: max_replicas=25, current_replicas=25, pending_pods=0. Logs show repeated create failures: 
```
E0123 14:02:10 controller.go:238] failed to create node: insufficient capacity scheduling tests, driver pod crashloop
```
Looks like driver/runtime instability is causing nodes to not join.

samir: stacking with CUDA/Xid errors in driver logs on the nodes that flapped. Example from /var/log/nvidia-container.log: 
```
[2025-07-10T13:59:01Z] Xid 31 at 0x7f2a... GPU fault: out of memory during kernel launch
[2025-07-10T13:59:02Z] GPU reset required, container oom kill
```
Node shows repeated kernel OOMs, kubelet marking NotReady, node removed from pool.

maria: confirmed — driver daemonset restart doesn't help long-term. suspect a kernel-driver regression introduced in yesterday's node image (ami-2025-0709).

jen: product here — which customers are impacted? any paying enterprise in-flight requests?

support-bot: Affected endpoints flagged via trace: enterprise-cust-42 (high priority), chat-proto-prod (low priority), free-account-batch (low priority). Estimated 4200 active requests failing or queued.

alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) increase autoscaler max_replicas to 40 (override) 2) temporarily route non-critical traffic to cpu-backup pool with smaller models 3) cordon flaky nodes and drain them 4) force restart nvidia-driver daemonset with older image 5) notify customers. I'll start overrides.

maria: +1 for routing low-priority to cpu-backup. Add a rate-limit to free tiers to preserve capacity for enterprise.

chris: Attempting autoscaler override now: 
```
# temp override
kubectl patch hpa gpu-autoscaler -n infra --type=json -p '[[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":40}]]'
```
Patch applied. HPA controller acknowledges new max. But note: nodes still failing to provision because driver image crashes on init.

samir: Driver downgrade queued — rolling nvidia-driver DS update to image `nvidia/driver:2025-06-28`. Applying now. This will force a rolling restart of driver pods on each node.

ops-bot: Deploy job started: deploy/driver-downgrade-2025-06-28. Status: in_progress.

alex: while driver rollback proceeds, enable a routing policy to offload low-priority routes. samir, can you flip the routing rule?

samir: flipping route: 
```
# redirect config
curl -XPOST https://control-plane/api/routes/override -d '{"match":{"tier":"free"},"route":"cpu-backup","timeout":30}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
Done. Confirmed ~57% of queued requests belonged to free tier; queue dropped ~45% in 2m.

jen: CSR team is on standby to reach out to enterprise-cust-42. I'll draft a status note and estimate ETA once we see driver rollback health.

maria: driver rollback progressing; 6/18 nodes updated, 3 nodes restarted by kubelet. But still seeing 3 nodes flapping with Xid 31 after restart — might be hardware or image mismatch.

chris: Querying k8s logs for node provisioning errors: 
```
E0720 14:18:43 node_controller.go: failed to register node: kubelet: runtime state invalid: container runtime crashed
```
Looks correlated to a specific AMI bake. We should consider moving those nodes to a spare instance group with a known-good AMI.

alex: I'm going to create a temporary nodegroup using ami-2025-0610 (previous stable) and increase cloud quota. Requesting cloud team to spin up 15 instances.

ops-bot: Cloud request submitted: request-33211. ETA ~4m for instance provisioning.

support-bot: Noted customer impact update posted to status page (internal draft). Enterprise-cust-42 is experiencing degraded responses.

jen: writing customer note: "We are actively mitigating GPU capacity issues; routing lower-priority traffic away and restoring driver image. Estimated partial recovery in 20–30m." Will send after alex confirms.

samir: new nodegroup coming up. Once nodes register, autoscaler should place pods there. Also enabling a temporary model-rollout to quantized variants for non-enterprise traffic to reduce memory pressure: 
```
PATCH /api/models/active
{"model":"gpt-small-q4","selector":{"tier":"free,low"}}
```
This reduced per-request GPU memory by ~30% in tests.

maria: good call. Doing a quick canary of the quantized model on cpu-backup first then shift to GPU as nodes come up.

chris: Cloud nodes are registering: 5/15 up, kubelet ready. Pods are scheduling. Queue depth down to 38%. Latency improving.

alex: driver rollback completed on 14/15 nodes, one node still flapping (marking NotReady). We'll cordon that one and exclude it from autoscaler.

maria: cordoned node ip 10.2.44.59. Draining may trigger job restarts; monitoring.

ops-bot: Cordon applied to node-10-2-44-59. Draining initiated.

support-bot: Sent status update to enterprise-cust-42: "We have applied mitigations (driver rollback, routing rules, temporary capacity increase). We expect further improvements within 15 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause analysis."

jen: customer replied: "Appetingly degraded but we can tolerate short bursts — keep us posted."

samir: Observability note: KV-cache hit rate decreased due to model switch; but overall token cost fell and tail latency improved. No new Xid errors seen on upgraded nodes.

chris: Autoscaler metrics show it attempted to scale to 38 and succeeded. Current_replicas=36. Scheduling backlog cleared to normal levels.

alex: oncall handoff — I need to go fix a downstream infra alert (networking). Maria will take lead for the incident timeline and postmortem. Handoff to @maria in 5.

maria: Acknowledged, taking lead. alex — leave any open ops steps in the incident doc please.

alex: leaving notes: 
- autoscaler max increased to 40 (temp)
- rolled back nvidia driver to 2025-06-28
- spun up temporary nodegroup using ami-2025-0610 (15 nodes)
- routed free/low tier to cpu-backup; quantized model applied to low tiers
- cordoned failing node 10.2.44.59
- customer notified: enterprise-cust-42

maria: Current status: mitigations improved capacity, queue normalized, no new kernel Xid faults on stable nodes. Severity downgraded to P2 in 22m. We'll keep monitoring for 2h.

jen: Thanks team. Please follow up with timeline and RCA steps. Support and product will coordinate customer comms.

samir: RCA hypothesis for now: regression in node image (ami-2025-0709) combined with a driver/kernel interaction causing GPU kernel OOMs under a specific load pattern. Postmortem action: revert AMI in autoscaling groups, add pre-deploy kernel-driver compatibility tests, add metric for node-level Xid errors to trigger auto-rollbacks.

maria: logging final incident note to incident tracker and scheduling a postmortem meeting tomorrow 1600 UTC. We will include: timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, long-term fixes (AMI rollback, driver validation, autoscaler resilient fallback).

ops-bot: Incident resolved: capacity restored, queue cleared. Resolution window: 1813456789 - 1813457389.

maria: closing thread here — postmortem to follow. Thanks all for quick response :thumbsup:
